description: ENHANCEMENT B: Expand the public-domain Strong's lexicon (deepresearch/fixtures/strongs.json) plus the verse/commentary fixtures (deepresearch/fixtures/commentary.json, and any remaining verses.json needs) so that the fixture-backed topics/anchors from FEAT-001 produce RICH, complete, schema-valid, well-sourced dossiers offline: more original_language_terms, more historical/commentary/cross-reference material. Keep all data strictly PUBLIC DOMAIN and keep the structure DATA-DRIVEN (no code changes needed to add data where possible; only make a minimal, tested parser change if a richer shape is truly warranted).
steps: Depends on FEAT-001. Re-read context.json keying rules. CRITICAL: strongs.json and commentary.json are keyed by the lookup key used in the pipeline: for a TOPIC query that key is the RAW query string (the exact phrasing passed, NOT normalized/lowercased); for a VERSE query it is the normalized reference. So to enrich a fixture-backed topic like 'judge not', add strongs.json/commentary.json entries keyed by BOTH the topic phrasing you test with (e.g. 'judge not') AND optionally the anchor reference (e.g. 'Matthew 7:1') if you also want verse-query runs to be rich. Match the existing fixture shapes exactly.

Grow deepresearch/fixtures/strongs.json: for the pivotal original-language terms of the FEAT-001 fixture-backed anchors, add entries following the existing shape (term [unicode Greek/Hebrew], transliteration, strongs [e.g. G#### / H####], language [greek/hebrew], definition, insight, source='Public-domain Strong's Greek lexicon' or Hebrew, locator=strongs number, optional url). Use ONLY public-domain Strong's content. Suggested pivotal terms: 'judge not'/Matthew 7:1 -> krino (G2919, 'to judge/condemn'); 'ask and it will be given'/Matthew 7:7 -> aiteo (G154, 'ask'), zeteo (G2212, 'seek'), krouo (G2925, 'knock'); 'narrow gate'/Matthew 7:13-14 -> stenos (G4728, 'narrow'), pyle (G4439, 'gate'); 'born again'/John 3:3 -> gennao (G1080, 'beget/be born'), anothen (G509, 'again / from above' - the key double meaning); 'i am the way the truth and the life'/John 14:6 -> hodos (G3598, 'way'), aletheia (G225, 'truth'), zoe (G2222, 'life'). Keep existing Matthew 5:17 and 'turn the other cheek' entries. Add Hebrew example(s) only if an added anchor is Old Testament (the seed set above is NT, so Greek is expected; keep the language enum values lowercase 'greek' which the connector maps to 'Greek').

Grow deepresearch/fixtures/commentary.json: for the fixture-backed topics/anchors, add entries following the existing shape, with 'kind' one of 'church-fathers' | 'historical' | 'cross-reference'. For church-fathers/commentary entries include excerpt, source, locator, and a url whose host is on the commentary allowlist (ccel.org/www.ccel.org, newadvent.org/www.newadvent.org, sacred-texts.com/www.sacred-texts.com, gutenberg.org/www.gutenberg.org) and whose path does NOT start with /search,/cgi-bin,/admin (off-allowlist or disallowed URLs are dropped by the connector - so keep them clean). For 'historical' entries use 'text' (no url needed). For 'cross-reference' entries include reference, text, source, locator. Key each entry list by the topic phrasing used in tests and/or the anchor reference, matching FEAT-001's fixture-backed subset. Keep all content strictly PUBLIC DOMAIN (Church Fathers, classic public-domain commentary, public-domain historical background). Preserve existing Matthew 5:17 and 'turn the other cheek' entries.

If any FEAT-001 fixture-backed anchor still lacks kjv/web/asv verse text in verses.json, add it here (same public-domain rule) so the end-to-end dossiers are complete. (Primary ownership of verses.json is FEAT-001; this step is a backstop.)

Confirm the connectors parse the enriched fixtures UNCHANGED: deepresearch/sources/strongs.py and commentary.py should need no code changes. Only if you deliberately introduce a richer JSON shape, make a MINIMAL, TESTED parser change and note it in findings. Do not break the language-enum mapping or the host/path allowlist behavior.

Add tests: in tests/test_sources.py (or a focused new test module following its patterns) assert that (a) the new Strong's terms surface for the new topics/anchors via StrongsConnector (term/strongs/definition present, language normalized to 'Greek'/'Hebrew'); (b) the new commentary/historical/cross-reference entries surface via CommentaryConnector and that any entry with an off-allowlist URL would be dropped (reuse the existing allowlist test pattern if present); (c) strongs.json, commentary.json, verses.json are all valid JSON. In tests/test_end_to_end.py, strengthen one or two FEAT-001 fixture-backed topic dossiers to additionally assert original_language_terms non-empty and commentary non-empty (richer offline output).
Run the offline suite and confirm green: `unset OPENAI_API_KEY ANTHROPIC_API_KEY && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q`. Do not weaken existing assertions.
Update README 'Sources (v1 wired)' area if useful to note the expanded lexicon/commentary coverage for the new topics.
acceptance_criteria: strongs.json, commentary.json, and verses.json remain valid JSON and are parsed unchanged by the existing connectors (or any parser change is minimal and covered by a new test).
The FEAT-001 fixture-backed topics now produce dossiers with non-empty original_language_terms and non-empty commentary offline.
New Strong's terms and commentary/historical/cross-reference entries are strictly public-domain and (for commentary URLs) on the host allowlist with allowed paths.
Running `unset OPENAI_API_KEY ANTHROPIC_API_KEY && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` passes with no network, including the new B tests, with no pre-existing test weakened.
verification: .venv/bin/python -m deepresearch research "born again" --dry-run --output-dir /tmp/dr_b && .venv/bin/python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('/tmp/dr_b/born-again.json'));assert d['original_language_terms'];assert d['commentary'];print('rich ok')"
findings: Enriched strongs.json and commentary.json for the FEAT-001 fixture-backed subset. strongs.json grew from 2 keys to 12: kept Matthew 5:17 and 'turn the other cheek'; added pivotal public-domain Strong's Greek terms keyed by BOTH the topic phrasing (raw query lookup) AND the anchor reference so topic and verse runs are both rich: 'judge not'/Matthew 7:1 -> krino G2919; 'ask and it will be given'/Matthew 7:7 -> aiteo G154, zeteo G2212, krouo G2925; 'narrow gate'/Matthew 7:13-14 -> stenos G4728, pyle G4439; 'born again'/John 3:3 -> gennao G1080, anothen G509; 'i am the way the truth and the life'/John 14:6 -> hodos G3598, aletheia G225, zoe G2222. All language values are lowercase 'greek' (connector maps to 'Greek'). commentary.json grew from 2 keys to 12 with the same keying; each fixture-backed topic/anchor now has church-fathers (allowlisted CCEL/New Advent URLs, allowed paths), historical ('text' only), and cross-reference ('reference'/'text'/'source'/'locator') entries. All content is strictly public domain (Chrysostom/Augustine patristics, classic commentary, public-domain historical background). verses.json needed NO backfill: FEAT-001 already covered all fixture-backed anchors. NO connector code change was needed; strongs.py and commentary.py parse the enriched fixtures unchanged (verified). Tests: added a parametrized test_strongs_connector_surfaces_new_terms (10 keys) and test_commentary_connector_surfaces_new_entries (10 keys) asserting term/definition/normalized-language presence and that every surfaced commentary URL is host+path allowed; added test_fixture_files_are_valid_json; strengthened the judge-not and born-again end-to-end dry-run tests to also assert original_language_terms and commentary are non-empty. No pre-existing assertion weakened. Offline suite: 79 passed (was 58), zero network, .venv 3.12. Dry-run verification for 'born again' confirms original_language_terms and commentary non-empty. NOTE: two unrelated pre-existing working-tree changes (task-deep-research-agent/task.json modification and two untracked review .md files) were left untouched and not staged; they are outside this feature's scope.
